title: Ἀπόλλων Ἕκτορα ἐξαρπάζει
about: Hector, seeing his brother Polydorus fall, can no longer keep away and comes at Achilles with his spear; Achilles leaps to meet him and says that this is the man who touched his heart most, who killed his companion. Hector answers that he will not be frightened by words, and that the outcome lies on the knees of the gods. He throws, but Athena breathes the spear back, and it falls at his feet. Achilles rushes on, and Apollo snatches Hector away in thick mist; three times Achilles strikes at the mist, and at the fourth rush he shouts that Hector has escaped death once more, but that he will finish him later if some god helps him too. Then he turns on the others: Dryops, Demuchus, Laogonus and Dardanus, Tros, who clasps his knees in vain, Mulius, Echeclus, Deucalion, Rhigmus and his driver Areithous. He is like a fire in a mountain forest, and like oxen treading barley: his horses trample dead men and shields, the chariot is spattered with blood, and his hands with gore.

sentences.t:
Ἕκτωρ δ’ ὡς ἐνόησε κασίγνητον Πολύδωρον
ἔντερα χερσὶν ἔχοντα λιαζόμενον ποτὶ γαίη
κάρ ῥά οἱ ὀφθαλμῶν κέχυτ’ ἀχλύς·
sentences.i: When Hector noticed his brother Polydorus holding his entrails in his hands and sinking to the ground, a haze was poured down over his eyes;
sentences.n: Hector is the subject of ἐνόησε ‘noticed’; ὡς … ἐνόησε is ‘when he noticed’, and the main clause only comes at the end of the third line. κασίγνητον Πολύδωρον ‘his brother Polydorus’ is the object, and ἔντερα χερσὶν ἔχοντα ‘holding his entrails in his hands’ and λιαζόμενον ποτὶ γαίη ‘bending down toward the ground’ (λιάζομαι ‘bend down’, ποτί = πρός) agree with it. κάρ is κατά with its last vowel dropped and its τ assimilated to the next consonant (ρ): κάρ … κέχυτ’ ‘down … was poured’, the pluperfect passive of χέω ‘pour’, with ὀφθαλμῶν ‘over his eyes’ (οἱ ‘for him’). ἀχλύς is ‘haze’. The paragraph break marks the new scene.

sentences.t:
οὐδ’ ἄρ’ ἔτ’ ἔτλη
δηρὸν ἑκὰς στρωφᾶσθ’, ἀλλ’ ἀντίος ἦλθ’ Ἀχιλῆϊ
ὀξὺ δόρυ κραδάων φλογὶ εἴκελος·
sentences.i: he could no longer bring himself to keep turning about far away, but came to meet Achilles, shaking a sharp spear, like a flame;
sentences.n: This unit begins in the middle of line 421. οὐδ’ ἄρ’ ἔτ’ ἔτλη ‘and no longer then did he bring himself’: ἔτλη is the aorist of τλάω ‘bear, bring oneself to’, and its infinitive is στρωφᾶσθ’ (στρωφάω ‘turn about’, middle), with δηρόν ‘for long’ and ἑκάς ‘far off, apart’. The ἀλλά clause has ἀντίος ἦλθ’ Ἀχιλῆϊ ‘opposite came to Achilles’ (dative). κραδάων is the present participle of κραδάω ‘shake, brandish’, with ὀξὺ δόρυ ‘a sharp spear’. φλογὶ εἴκελος ‘like flame’ takes the dative; it says how he looked, not what he did.

sentences.t:
αὐτὰρ Ἀχιλλεὺς
ὡς εἶδ’, ὣς ἀνεπᾶλτο, καὶ εὐχόμενος ἔπος ηὔδα·
sentences.l:
but Achilles
as he saw him, so he leapt up, and, declaring, spoke a word:
sentences.i: and Achilles, as soon as he saw him, leapt up, and said, declaring aloud:
sentences.n: This unit begins in the middle of line 423 with αὐτάρ ‘but’. ὡς εἶδ’, ὣς ἀνεπᾶλτο ‘as he saw him, so he leapt up’ is a pair of correlatives (ὡς … ὣς ‘as … so’, ‘no sooner … than’): εἶδ’ is the aorist of ὁράω, ἀνεπᾶλτο the aorist of ἀναπάλλομαι ‘leap up’. καὶ εὐχόμενος ἔπος ηὔδα ‘and declaring spoke a word’: εὔχομαι is ‘declare’ of a vaunt here, not ‘pray’. The colon introduces the speech.

sentences.t:
ἐγγὺς ἀνὴρ ὃς ἐμόν γε μάλιστ’ ἐσεμάσσατο θυμόν,
ὅς μοι ἑταῖρον ἔπεφνε τετιμένον· οὐδ’ ἂν ἔτι δὴν
ἀλλήλους πτώσσοιμεν ἀνὰ πτολέμοιο γεφύρας.
sentences.l:
“Near is the man who most of all touched my heart,
who killed my honoured companion; nor would we any longer for long
cower from each other along the bridges of war.”
sentences.i: “Near is the man who touched my heart most, who killed my honoured companion; and we shall not go on cowering from each other much longer along the bridges of war.”
sentences.n: ἐγγὺς ἀνήρ ‘near is the man’ has no verb. ὃς ἐμόν γε μάλιστ’ ἐσεμάσσατο θυμόν ‘who most of all touched my heart’: ἐσεμάσσατο is a rare aorist (ἐς- + the aorist of μαίομαι ‘touch’; the sense ‘moved’ is taken from the context). ὅς μοι ἑταῖρον ἔπεφνε τετιμένον ‘who killed my honoured companion’: ἔπεφνε is the aorist of φένω ‘kill’, and τετιμένον is the perfect passive participle of τιμάω ‘honour’ — Patroclus. οὐδ’ ἂν ἔτι δὴν … πτώσσοιμεν ‘nor would we any longer for long cower’ is the optative with ἄν (a mild future); ἀλλήλους ‘each other’. ἀνὰ πτολέμοιο γεφύρας ‘along the bridges of war’: the meaning of γεφύρας here is not known.

sentences.t: ἦ, καὶ ὑπόδρα ἰδὼν προσεφώνεεν Ἕκτορα δῖον·
sentences.l: He spoke, and with a scowl looking at him addressed Hector the heavenly:
sentences.i: So he said, and looking at heavenly Hector with a scowl, spoke to him:
sentences.n: ἦ, καί ‘he spoke, and’ closes the speech and starts the action; ἦ is the old ‘he said’, kept apart from ὣς φάτο. ὑπόδρα ἰδών ‘looking with a scowl’ is a stock phrase (the derivation of ὑπόδρα is not certain), and προσεφώνεεν is the imperfect of προσφωνέω ‘address’ with the accusative Ἕκτορα δῖον ‘Hector the heavenly’. The paragraph break marks a new beat in Achilles’ challenge, not a new speaker.

sentences.t: ἆσσον ἴθ’ ὥς κεν θᾶσσον ὀλέθρου πείραθ’ ἵκηαι.
sentences.l: “Nearer come, so that sooner the limits of destruction you may reach.”
sentences.i: “Come nearer, so that you may reach the limits of destruction the sooner.”
sentences.n: A one-line speech. ἆσσον is the comparative ‘nearer’, ἴθ’ the imperative of εἶμι ‘go, come’. ὥς κεν … ἵκηαι ‘so that … you may reach’ is a purpose clause: ἵκηαι is the aorist subjunctive of ἱκνέομαι with κεν. θᾶσσον is the comparative of ταχύς ‘sooner’; ὀλέθρου πείραθ’ is ‘the limits of destruction’. The same line closes a longer speech elsewhere, where the sentence is completed by the lines before it.

sentences.t: τὸν δ’ οὐ ταρβήσας προσέφη κορυθαίολος Ἕκτωρ·
sentences.l: Him then, not terrified, addressed Hector of the glancing helmet:
sentences.i: Then Hector of the glancing helmet, unafraid, spoke to him:
sentences.n: A reply-formula: τὸν δ’ ‘him then’ is Achilles. ταρβήσας is the aorist participle of ταρβέω ‘be terrified’, and with οὐ it means ‘not terrified’. κορυθαίολος Ἕκτωρ ‘Hector of the glancing helmet’ is a stock epithet, translated every time (κόρυς ‘helmet’ + αἰόλος ‘quick-moving, glancing’). The paragraph break marks the change of speaker.

sentences.t:
Πηλεΐδη μὴ δὴ ἐπέεσσί με νηπύτιον ὣς
ἔλπεο δειδίξεσθαι, ἐπεὶ σάφα οἶδα καὶ αὐτὸς
ἠμὲν κερτομίας ἠδ’ αἴσυλα μυθήσασθαι.
sentences.l:
“Son of Peleus, do not indeed with words me, like a babe,
hope to frighten, since clearly I know, even myself,
both taunts and wicked things to speak.
sentences.i: “Son of Peleus, do not hope to frighten me with words as though I were a child, since I too know well how to speak both taunts and wicked things.
sentences.n: Πηλεΐδη is the vocative of the patronymic ‘son of Peleus’. μὴ … ἔλπεο is a prohibition (ἔλπομαι ‘hope’, imperative), with the infinitive δειδίξεσθαι ‘to frighten’ (from δειδίσσομαι); ἐπέεσσι is ‘with words’ and με the object. νηπύτιον ὣς ‘like a babe’ (νηπύτιος ‘childish, a babe’). ἐπεὶ σάφα οἶδα καὶ αὐτός ‘since clearly I know, even myself’: σάφα is an adverb, and καὶ αὐτός means ‘I too’. ἠμὲν … ἠδ’ is ‘both … and’; κερτομίας is ‘taunts’ and αἴσυλα ‘wicked things’; μυθήσασθαι is the aorist infinitive ‘to speak’.

sentences.t: οἶδα δ’ ὅτι σὺ μὲν ἐσθλός, ἐγὼ δὲ σέθεν πολὺ χείρων.
sentences.l: And I know that you indeed are good, and I far worse than you.
sentences.i: I know that you are a good man, and that I am far worse than you.
sentences.n: οἶδα δ’ ὅτι ‘and I know that’; σὺ μὲν ἐσθλός, ἐγὼ δὲ σέθεν πολὺ χείρων sets the two men against each other with μέν … δέ. ἐσθλός is ‘good’ (of fighting worth), χείρων the comparative of κακός ‘worse’, with the genitive of comparison σέθεν ‘than you’ (epic for σοῦ) and πολύ ‘by much’.

sentences.t:
ἀλλ’ ἤτοι μὲν ταῦτα θεῶν ἐν γούνασι κεῖται,
αἴ κέ σε χειρότερός περ ἐὼν ἀπὸ θυμὸν ἕλωμαι
δουρὶ βαλών, ἐπεὶ ἦ καὶ ἐμὸν βέλος ὀξὺ πάροιθεν.
sentences.l:
But indeed these things lie on the knees of the gods,
if perhaps I, though being worse, your life from you take away
having struck with a spear, since indeed my missile too is sharp in front.”
sentences.i: But these things lie on the knees of the gods, to see if I, though the worse man, may take your life from you by striking you with my spear, since my weapon too is sharp at its front.”
sentences.n: ταῦτα θεῶν ἐν γούνασι κεῖται ‘these things lie on the knees of the gods’ is a saying for ‘it rests with the gods’. αἴ κέ … ἕλωμαι ‘if perhaps I take’ (αἴ = εἰ) is the aorist subjunctive of αἱρέω, with ἀπό in tmesis: ἀπὸ θυμὸν ἕλωμαι ‘take your life away’, where σε ‘you’ is a second accusative (‘take from you your life’). χειρότερός περ ἐών ‘though being worse’ (comparative of κακός, as χείρων above). δουρὶ βαλών ‘having struck with a spear’. ἐπεὶ ἦ καὶ ἐμὸν βέλος ὀξὺ πάροιθεν ‘since indeed my missile too is sharp in front’: βέλος is any missile, here a spear, and πάροιθεν ‘in front’ means at the point. Hector’s speech ends here.

sentences.t:
ἦ ῥα, καὶ ἀμπεπαλὼν προΐει δόρυ, καὶ τό γ’ Ἀθήνη
πνοιῇ Ἀχιλλῆος πάλιν ἔτραπε κυδαλίμοιο
ἦκα μάλα ψύξασα·
sentences.i: So he said, and brandishing it he sent forth his spear, but Athena turned it back from glorious Achilles with a breath, breathing on it very softly;
sentences.n: ἦ ῥα, καί ‘he spoke, and’. ἀμπεπαλών is the aorist participle of ἀναπάλλω ‘brandish’ and προΐει the imperfect of προΐημι ‘send forth’. καὶ τό γ’ Ἀθήνη … πάλιν ἔτραπε ‘and that Athena turned back’: τό is the spear, and ἔτραπε is the aorist of τρέπω ‘turn’. πνοιῇ ‘with a breath’ is dative; Ἀχιλλῆος … κυδαλίμοιο ‘from glorious Achilles’ is genitive of separation. ἦκα μάλα ψύξασα ‘very softly having breathed’: ψύξασα is the aorist participle of ψύχω ‘breathe’ and ἦκα is ‘softly’.

sentences.t:
τὸ δ’ ἂψ ἵκεθ’ Ἕκτορα δῖον,
αὐτοῦ δὲ προπάροιθε ποδῶν πέσεν.
sentences.l:
and it came back to Hector the heavenly,
and on the spot before his feet it fell.
sentences.i: and it came back to heavenly Hector and fell on the spot in front of his feet.
sentences.n: This unit begins in the middle of line 440. τὸ δ’ is the spear; ἂψ ἵκεθ’ is ‘came back’ (ἵκεθ’ = ἵκετο, the aorist of ἱκνέομαι ‘come to’), with Ἕκτορα δῖον ‘Hector the heavenly’. αὐτοῦ is the adverb ‘on the spot’, and προπάροιθε ποδῶν ‘in front of his feet’ takes the genitive; πέσεν is the aorist of πίπτω ‘fall’.

sentences.t:
αὐτὰρ Ἀχιλλεὺς
ἐμμεμαὼς ἐπόρουσε κατακτάμεναι μενεαίνων,
σμερδαλέα ἰάχων·
sentences.i: and Achilles rushed on in his eagerness to kill him, crying out terribly;
sentences.n: This unit begins in the middle of line 441 with αὐτὰρ Ἀχιλλεύς ‘but Achilles’. ἐμμεμαώς is the perfect participle of μέμονα ‘be eager’ (ἐν- + μεμαώς), ἐπόρουσε the aorist of ἐπορούω ‘rush on’, and κατακτάμεναι an aorist infinitive of κατακτείνω ‘kill’, giving the purpose. μενεαίνων ‘full of eagerness’ is a second participle for the same feeling (μενεαίνω ‘be eager’), so i says it once. σμερδαλέα ἰάχων ‘terribly crying out’: the neuter plural σμερδαλέα is an adverb.

sentences.t:
τὸν δ’ ἐξήρπαξεν Ἀπόλλων
ῥεῖα μάλ’ ὥς τε θεός, ἐκάλυψε δ’ ἄρ’ ἠέρι πολλῇ.
sentences.l:
but him snatched away Apollo
very easily, like a god, and covered him then with thick mist.
sentences.i: but Apollo snatched him away, with all the ease of a god, and covered him in thick mist.
sentences.n: This unit begins in the middle of line 443. τὸν δ’ is Hector, and ἐξήρπαξεν the aorist of ἐξαρπάζω ‘snatch away’; Ἀπόλλων stands last in the line. ῥεῖα μάλ’ ὥς τε θεός ‘very easily, like a god’ (ῥεῖα = ῥέα ‘easily’). ἐκάλυψε δ’ ἄρ’ ἠέρι πολλῇ ‘and covered him then with thick mist’: ἠήρ is ‘mist’, and πολλῇ ‘thick’ is from πολύς. The words from ῥεῖα on are the ones used of Aphrodite taking Paris from the duel.

sentences.t:
τρὶς μὲν ἔπειτ’ ἐπόρουσε ποδάρκης δῖος Ἀχιλλεὺς
ἔγχεϊ χαλκείῳ, τρὶς δ’ ἠέρα τύψε βαθεῖαν.
sentences.l:
Three times then rushed on swift-footed, heavenly Achilles
with his bronze spear, and three times he struck the deep mist.
sentences.i: Three times, then, swift-footed, heavenly Achilles rushed on with his bronze spear, and three times he struck the deep mist.
sentences.n: τρὶς μὲν … τρὶς δ’ ‘three times … and three times’ sets the two halves side by side. ἐπόρουσε is the aorist of ἐπορούω ‘rush on’. ποδάρκης δῖος Ἀχιλλεύς ‘swift-footed, heavenly Achilles’: ποδάρκης is a stock epithet whose formation is uncertain (probably πούς + ἀρκέω), translated every time and kept apart from ποδώκης ‘fleet-footed’. ἔγχεϊ χαλκείῳ ‘with his bronze spear’ is dative; τύψε is the aorist of τύπτω ‘strike’; ἠέρα … βαθεῖαν is ‘the deep mist’.

sentences.t:
ἀλλ’ ὅτε δὴ τὸ τέταρτον ἐπέσσυτο δαίμονι ἶσος,
δεινὰ δ’ ὁμοκλήσας ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα·
sentences.l:
But when for the fourth time he rushed on, equal to a divinity,
and dreadfully having shouted at him, winged words he spoke:
sentences.i: But when he rushed on for the fourth time, like a divinity, he shouted dreadfully at him and spoke winged words:
sentences.n: ἀλλ’ ὅτε δὴ ‘but when’; τὸ τέταρτον ‘for the fourth time’ is the neuter used as an adverb; ἐπέσσυτο is the aorist of ἐπισεύομαι ‘rush on’; δαίμονι ἶσος ‘equal to a divinity’ (the dative with ἶσος). δεινὰ δ’ ὁμοκλήσας ‘and dreadfully having shouted at him’: δεινά is a neuter plural used as an adverb, ὁμοκλήσας the aorist participle of ὁμοκλάω ‘shout at’. ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα ‘he spoke winged words’ is the stock speech-introduction, translated every time. The subject is still Achilles.

sentences.t:
ἐξ αὖ νῦν ἔφυγες θάνατον κύον· ἦ τέ τοι ἄγχι
ἦλθε κακόν·
sentences.l:
“Out again now you fled death, dog; truly, near to you
came evil;
sentences.i: “Once more you have escaped death, you dog; evil came very near to you;
sentences.n: ἐξ … ἔφυγες ‘out … you fled’ (‘you have escaped’ in i), the aorist of φεύγω with ἐκ in tmesis, takes θάνατον ‘death’ as its object. νῦν αὖ is ‘now again’. κύον is the vocative of κύων ‘dog’. ἦ τέ τοι ἄγχι ἦλθε κακόν ‘truly near you came evil’: ἄγχι ‘near’ governs τοι (= σοι), and ἦλθε is the aorist of ἔρχομαι. The direct speech starts here; the quotation mark opens on this unit.

sentences.t:
νῦν αὖτέ σ’ ἐρύσατο Φοῖβος Ἀπόλλων,
ᾧ μέλλεις εὔχεσθαι ἰὼν ἐς δοῦπον ἀκόντων.
sentences.l:
now again Phoebus Apollo has guarded you,
to whom you are sure to pray, going into the crash of javelins.
sentences.i: now again Phoebus Apollo has protected you, to whom you must pray when you go into the crash of javelins.
sentences.n: This unit begins in the middle of line 450. νῦν αὖτέ σ’ ἐρύσατο ‘now again … has guarded you’: ἐρύσατο is the aorist middle of ἐρύομαι ‘guard, protect’. Φοῖβος Ἀπόλλων is ‘Phoebus Apollo’. ᾧ μέλλεις εὔχεσθαι ‘to whom you are sure to pray’: ᾧ is the relative ‘to whom’, μέλλεις with the infinitive means ‘be sure to’ (not ‘be about to’). ἰὼν ἐς δοῦπον ἀκόντων ‘going into the crash of javelins’ (δοῦπος ‘thud, crash’).

sentences.t:
ἦ θήν σ’ ἐξανύω γε καὶ ὕστερον ἀντιβολήσας,
εἴ πού τις καὶ ἔμοιγε θεῶν ἐπιτάρροθός ἐστι.
sentences.l:
Surely I shall finish you off, at least, even later, having met you,
if perhaps some one of the gods is a helper to me too.
sentences.i: I shall surely finish you off even later, when I meet you, if perhaps some one of the gods is a helper to me too.
sentences.n: ἦ θήν is ‘surely’, with ἐξανύω γε ‘I shall finish you off’ (present with the force of a future; ἐξανύω ‘make an end of’). καὶ ὕστερον ‘even later’; ἀντιβολήσας is the aorist participle of ἀντιβολέω ‘meet’. εἴ πού τις … ἐστι ‘if perhaps some one … is’, with ἔμοιγε ‘to me too’ (καί ‘too’), and ἐπιτάρροθος ‘helper’, a rare word.

sentences.t: νῦν αὖ τοὺς ἄλλους ἐπιείσομαι, ὅν κε κιχείω.
sentences.l: Now in turn the others I shall go against, whomever I may reach.”
sentences.i: Now I shall go after the others, whoever I can reach.”
sentences.n: νῦν αὖ ‘now in turn’ turns from Hector to the rest. ἐπιείσομαι is the future of ἐπίειμι ‘go against, go after’, with τοὺς ἄλλους ‘the others’. ὅν κε κιχείω ‘whomever I may reach’: κιχείω is the aorist subjunctive of κιχάνω ‘reach’, with κε. Achilles’ speech ends here.

sentences.t: ὣς εἰπὼν Δρύοπ’ οὖτα κατ’ αὐχένα μέσσον ἄκοντι·
sentences.l: So having spoken, Dryops he wounded in the neck, in the middle, with a javelin;
sentences.i: So he spoke, and stabbed Dryops with his javelin in the middle of the neck;
sentences.n: ὣς εἰπών ‘so having spoken’. Δρύοπ’ is the accusative of Δρύοψ, ‘Dryops’, a man not otherwise described here. οὖτα is the aorist of οὐτάω ‘wound with a thrust’ (‘stabbed’ in i), κατ’ αὐχένα μέσσον ‘in the middle of the neck’ (αὐχήν ‘neck’), ἄκοντι ‘with a javelin’. The paragraph break marks the start of the killing list.

sentences.t:
ἤριπε δὲ προπάροιθε ποδῶν· ὃ δὲ τὸν μὲν ἔασε,
Δημοῦχον δὲ Φιλητορίδην ἠΰν τε μέγαν τε
κὰγ γόνυ δουρὶ βαλὼν ἠρύκακε.
sentences.l:
and he crashed down before his feet; and he left him,
and Demuchus, the son of Philetor, both good and big,
in the knee having struck with a spear, held back.
sentences.i: Dryops crashed down in front of Achilles’ feet, and Achilles left him lying; but Demuchus, the son of Philetor, good and big, he struck in the knee with a spear and held back.
sentences.n: ἤριπε is the aorist of ἐρείπω ‘crash down’, subject Dryops; προπάροιθε ποδῶν ‘in front of his feet’. ὃ δὲ τὸν μὲν ἔασε ‘and he (Achilles) left him’: ἔασε is the aorist of ἐάω ‘leave, let be’, and τόν is Dryops. Δημοῦχον δὲ Φιλητορίδην ‘and Demuchus, the son of Philetor’ (a patronymic); ἠΰν τε μέγαν τε ‘both good and big’ (ἠΰς is the epic ἐΰς ‘good’). κὰγ γόνυ is κατὰ γόνυ ‘in the knee’ (the τ of κατά assimilated to the γ), δουρὶ βαλών ‘having struck with a spear’. ἠρύκακε is a reduplicated aorist of ἐρύκω ‘hold back’.

sentences.t:
τὸν μὲν ἔπειτα
οὐτάζων ξίφεϊ μεγάλῳ ἐξαίνυτο θυμόν·
sentences.l:
him then
thrusting at with a great sword he took away his life;
sentences.i: then, stabbing him with a great sword, he took his life from him;
sentences.n: This unit begins in the middle of line 458. τὸν μὲν ἔπειτα ‘him then’ is Demuchus. οὐτάζων is the present participle of οὐτάζω ‘thrust at, stab’; ξίφεϊ μεγάλῳ ‘with a great sword’ (dative). ἐξαίνυτο θυμόν ‘took away his life’: ἐξαίνυτο is the imperfect middle of ἐξαινύμαι ‘take away’, and θυμός of the life that leaves the body is ‘life’.

sentences.t:
αὐτὰρ ὃ Λαόγονον καὶ Δάρδανον υἷε Βίαντος
ἄμφω ἐφορμηθεὶς ἐξ ἵππων ὦσε χαμᾶζε,
τὸν μὲν δουρὶ βαλών, τὸν δὲ σχεδὸν ἄορι τύψας.
sentences.l:
but he Laogonus and Dardanus, the two sons of Bias,
both, having rushed on, from the horses thrust to the ground,
the one with a spear having struck, the other near at hand with a sword having struck.
sentences.i: Then he rushed upon Laogonus and Dardanus, the two sons of Bias, and pushed them both from their chariot to the ground, striking the one with a spear and the other at close quarters with a sword.
sentences.n: Λαόγονον καὶ Δάρδανον υἷε Βίαντος: υἷε is the dual ‘two sons’ (υἱός), with Βίαντος ‘of Bias’; the two men are the object of ὦσε ‘thrust’ (aorist of ὠθέω), ἄμφω ‘both’. ἐφορμηθείς is the aorist participle, passive in form and middle in sense, of ἐφορμάομαι ‘rush on’; it goes with the subject, and ἄμφω ‘both’ with the two men. ἐξ ἵππων ‘from the horses’ means out of the chariot they drive. χαμᾶζε ‘to the ground’. τὸν μὲν … τὸν δέ ‘the one … the other’; βαλών and τύψας are aorist participles of βάλλω and τύπτω, both ‘strike’; σχεδόν ‘near, at close quarters’, ἄορι ‘with a sword’ (ἄορ is a second word for sword).

sentences.t:
Τρῶα δ’ Ἀλαστορίδην, ὃ μὲν ἀντίος ἤλυθε γούνων,
εἴ πώς εὑ πεφίδοιτο λαβὼν καὶ ζωὸν ἀφείη
μηδὲ κατακτείνειεν ὁμηλικίην ἐλεήσας,
sentences.i: Tros, the son of Alastor, came up facing Achilles’ knees, hoping that Achilles would somehow take him, spare him, and let him go alive, and not kill him, pitying a man of his own age —
sentences.n: Τρῶα δ’ Ἀλαστορίδην ‘and Tros, Alastor’s son’ (patronymic) is put first, and is picked up by ὃ μὲν and, as the object of οὖτα, at 469. ἀντίος ἤλυθε γούνων ‘came opposite to his knees’: γούνων is the genitive after ἀντίος ‘facing’, the posture of one who would clasp the knees. εἴ πώς εὑ πεφίδοιτο … ‘if in some way he would spare him’: a wish put as a condition; πεφίδοιτο is the aorist optative of φείδομαι ‘spare’, εὑ = ἑ ‘him’, λαβών ‘having taken (him)’. ζωὸν ἀφείη ‘let him go alive’ (ἀφείη the aorist optative of ἀφίημι), μηδὲ κατακτείνειεν ‘and not kill him’. ὁμηλικίην is the abstract noun ‘equality of age’, used for the person: ‘one of his own age’; ἐλεήσας ‘having pitied’ (aorist participle of ἐλεέω).

sentences.t: νήπιος, οὐδὲ τὸ ᾔδη ὃ οὐ πείσεσθαι ἔμελλεν·
sentences.l: foolish, nor did he know this, that he was not to be won over;
sentences.i: foolish as he was, he did not know that Achilles was not to be won over;
sentences.n: νήπιος ‘foolish’ is nominative, said of Tros. οὐδὲ τὸ ᾔδη ‘nor did he know this’: ᾔδη is the pluperfect of οἶδα, used as a past ‘knew’. ὃ οὐ πείσεσθαι ἔμελλεν ‘that he was not to be won over’: ὅ is ‘that’, πείσεσθαι the future infinitive of πείθομαι ‘be persuaded’, and ἔμελλεν ‘was going to’; the person who would not be won over is Achilles. The line is also found in the Odyssey, there with Athena as the one not won over.

sentences.t:
οὐ γάρ τι γλυκύθυμος ἀνὴρ ἦν οὐδ’ ἀγανόφρων,
ἀλλὰ μάλ’ ἐμμεμαώς·
sentences.l:
for he was not at all a sweet-hearted man, nor gentle-minded,
but very eager;
sentences.i: for he was not at all a man of tender heart or gentle mind, but very eager;
sentences.n: οὐ γάρ τι ‘for not at all’. γλυκύθυμος is ‘sweet-hearted’ (γλυκύς + θυμός ‘heart’) and ἀγανόφρων ‘gentle-minded’ (ἀγανός ‘gentle’ + φρήν ‘mind’) (both rare words). ἀλλὰ μάλ’ ἐμμεμαώς ‘but very eager’, the perfect participle of μέμονα, as at 442; the thing he was eager for is left unsaid.

sentences.t:
ὃ μὲν ἥπτετο χείρεσι γούνων
ἱέμενος λίσσεσθ’, ὃ δὲ φασγάνῳ οὖτα καθ’ ἧπαρ·
sentences.l:
the one laid hold of his knees with his hands,
eager to beseech him, and the other with a sword wounded him down in the liver;
sentences.i: Tros was clasping his knees with his hands, eager to plead, but Achilles stabbed him in the liver with his sword;
sentences.n: This unit begins in the middle of line 468. ὃ μέν … ὃ δέ ‘the one … the other’, Tros and Achilles. ἥπτετο is the imperfect of ἅπτομαι ‘lay hold of’ and takes γούνων ‘his knees’ (genitive); χείρεσι is ‘with his hands’. ἱέμενος λίσσεσθ’ ‘eager to beseech’ (ἵεμαι ‘be eager’, λίσσομαι ‘beg’). φασγάνῳ ‘with a sword’ (φάσγανον). οὖτα καθ’ ἧπαρ ‘wounded him in the liver’ (κατά + ἧπαρ, the liver).

sentences.t:
ἐκ δέ οἱ ἧπαρ ὄλισθεν, ἀτὰρ μέλαν αἷμα κατ’ αὐτοῦ
κόλπον ἐνέπλησεν·
sentences.l:
and out of him the liver slipped, and dark blood down over him
filled his lap;
sentences.i: and the liver slipped out of him, and dark blood filled his lap, running down over him;
sentences.n: ἐκ δέ οἱ ἧπαρ ὄλισθεν ‘and out of him the liver slipped’: ὄλισθεν is the aorist of ὀλισθάνω ‘slip’, with ἐκ in tmesis and οἱ ‘from him’. ἀτάρ ‘and’. μέλαν αἷμα ‘dark blood’. κατ’ αὐτοῦ ‘down over him’ is κατά with the genitive of αὐτός. κόλπον ἐνέπλησεν ‘filled his lap’ (κόλπος ‘lap, fold’), the aorist of ἐμπίμπλημι; the subject is the blood.

sentences.t:
τὸν δὲ σκότος ὄσσε κάλυψε
θυμοῦ δευόμενον·
sentences.l:
and darkness covered his two eyes,
lacking life;
sentences.i: and darkness covered his eyes as he lacked life;
sentences.n: τὸν δέ is Tros. σκότος ὄσσε κάλυψε ‘darkness covered his eyes’: ὄσσε is the dual ‘both eyes’, and κάλυψε is the aorist of καλύπτω. θυμοῦ δευόμενον ‘lacking life’: δεύομαι ‘lack’ takes the genitive, and θυμοῦ is ‘of life’. The unit begins in the middle of line 471 and ends in the middle of 472.

sentences.t:
ὃ δὲ Μούλιον οὖτα παραστὰς
δουρὶ κατ’ οὖς· εἶθαρ δὲ δι’ οὔατος ἦλθ’ ἑτέροιο
αἰχμὴ χαλκείη·
sentences.i: And standing beside Mulius, he stabbed him with his spear in the ear, and at once the bronze point went through the other ear;
sentences.n: This unit begins in the middle of line 472. ὃ δέ is Achilles; Μούλιον is ‘Mulius’. οὖτα παραστάς ‘wounded standing beside him’ (παραστάς the aorist participle of παρίστημι); δουρὶ κατ’ οὖς ‘with a spear at the ear’. εἶθαρ is ‘straightway’. δι’ οὔατος ἦλθ’ ἑτέροιο ‘went through the other ear’ (οὖς, οὔατος ‘ear’; ἕτερος ‘the other’). αἰχμὴ χαλκείη ‘the bronze point’, held to the end.

sentences.t:
ὃ δ’ Ἀγήνορος υἱὸν Ἔχεκλον
μέσσην κὰκ κεφαλὴν ξίφει ἤλασε κωπήεντι,
sentences.l:
and he Agenor’s son Echeclus
in the middle of the head with a hilted sword struck,
sentences.i: and he struck Echeclus, the son of Agenor, on the middle of the head with his hilted sword,
sentences.n: This unit begins in the middle of line 474. Ἀγήνορος υἱὸν Ἔχεκλον ‘Agenor’s son Echeclus’. μέσσην κὰκ κεφαλήν is μέσσην κατὰ κεφαλήν ‘on the middle of the head’ (κὰκ, the τ of κατά assimilated to the κ). ἤλασε is the aorist of ἐλαύνω, ‘drive’ of a sword-stroke, and here ‘struck’; ξίφει κωπήεντι is ‘with a hilted sword’ (κώπη ‘hilt’).

sentences.t: πᾶν δ’ ὑπεθερμάνθη ξίφος αἵματι·
sentences.l: and the whole sword grew warm beneath with blood;
sentences.i: and the whole sword grew warm with blood;
sentences.n: πᾶν … ξίφος ‘the whole sword’; ὑπεθερμάνθη is the aorist passive of ὑποθερμαίνομαι ‘grow warm beneath’, with the prefix shown as ‘beneath’ in l and not shown in i. αἵματι ‘with blood’ is dative. The unit ends in the middle of line 476.

sentences.t:
τὸν δὲ κατ’ ὄσσε
ἔλλαβε πορφύρεος θάνατος καὶ μοῖρα κραταιή.
sentences.l:
and him, down over the eyes,
seized purple death and strong fate.
sentences.i: and purple death and strong fate seized him, down over his eyes.
sentences.n: This unit begins in the middle of line 476. τὸν δὲ κατ’ ὄσσε ἔλλαβε ‘and him, down over the eyes, seized’: τόν is Echeclus, ὄσσε the dual ‘eyes’, κατά ‘down over’, and ἔλλαβε the aorist of λαμβάνω. πορφύρεος θάνατος καὶ μοῖρα κραταιή ‘purple death and strong fate’ is a stock phrase, translated every time (κραταιός is ‘strong’ like κρατερός).

sentences.t:
Δευκαλίωνα δ’ ἔπειθ’, ἵνα τε ξυνέχουσι τένοντες
ἀγκῶνος, τῇ τόν γε φίλης διὰ χειρὸς ἔπειρεν
αἰχμῇ χαλκείῃ·
sentences.i: Then Deucalion: where the tendons of the elbow hold together, there he pierced him right through the hand with a bronze point;
sentences.n: Δευκαλίωνα is the accusative of Δευκαλίων ‘Deucalion’. ἵνα τε ξυνέχουσι τένοντες ἀγκῶνος ‘where the tendons hold the elbow together’ (ξυν- = συν-; τένων ‘tendon’; ἀγκών ‘elbow’). τῇ τόν γε … ἔπειρεν ‘there … he pierced him’: ἔπειρεν is the imperfect of πείρω ‘pierce through’, with φίλης διὰ χειρός ‘through his hand’ (φίλος ‘own, dear’). αἰχμῇ χαλκείῃ ‘with a bronze point’. The unit ends in the middle of line 480.

sentences.t:
ὃ δέ μιν μένε χεῖρα βαρυνθεὶς
πρόσθ’ ὁρόων θάνατον·
sentences.l:
and he waited for him, weighed down as to the hand,
looking at death before him;
sentences.i: and Deucalion, his hand weighed down, waited for him, seeing death before him;
sentences.n: This unit begins in the middle of line 480. ὃ δέ μιν μένε ‘and he waited for him’: μένε is the imperfect of μένω, μιν ‘him’, Achilles. χεῖρα βαρυνθείς ‘weighed down as to the hand’: βαρυνθείς is the aorist passive participle of βαρύνω ‘weigh down’, with χεῖρα an accusative of respect. πρόσθ’ ὁρόων θάνατον ‘looking at death before him’ (ὁρόων the epic present participle of ὁράω).

sentences.t:
ὃ δὲ φασγάνῳ αὐχένα θείνας
τῆλ’ αὐτῇ πήληκι κάρη βάλε·
sentences.l:
and he, his neck having struck with a sword,
far off with the helmet itself his head cast;
sentences.i: and Achilles struck Deucalion’s neck with his sword and cast his head far off, helmet and all;
sentences.n: This unit begins in the middle of line 481. ὃ δὲ … θείνας ‘and he … having struck’: θείνας is the aorist participle of θείνω ‘strike’, with αὐχένα ‘neck’ and φασγάνῳ ‘with a sword’. τῆλε (here τῆλ’) is ‘far off’. αὐτῇ πήληκι ‘with the helmet itself’ means helmet and all (πήληξ ‘helmet’); κάρη βάλε ‘cast his head’ (κάρη, a neuter noun, ‘head’; βάλε the aorist of βάλλω).

sentences.t:
μυελὸς αὖτε
σφονδυλίων ἔκπαλθ’, ὃ δ’ ἐπὶ χθονὶ κεῖτο τανυσθείς.
sentences.l:
the marrow in turn
from the vertebrae sprang out, and he on the ground lay stretched out.
sentences.i: the marrow sprang out of his vertebrae, and he lay stretched out on the ground.
sentences.n: This unit begins in the middle of line 482. μυελός ‘marrow’; αὖτε ‘in turn, then’; σφονδυλίων is the genitive plural of σφονδύλιον ‘vertebra’. ἔκπαλθ’ is the aorist of ἐκπάλλομαι ‘spring out’ (a short form, ἔκπαλτο). ὃ δ’ is the headless body: ἐπὶ χθονὶ κεῖτο τανυσθείς ‘lay on the ground stretched out’ (κεῖτο the imperfect of κεῖμαι, τανυσθείς the aorist passive participle of τανύω ‘stretch’).

sentences.t:
αὐτὰρ ὃ βῆ ῥ’ ἰέναι μετ’ ἀμύμονα Πείρεω υἱὸν
Ῥίγμον, ὃς ἐκ Θρῄκης ἐριβώλακος εἰληλούθει·
sentences.l:
But he set out to go after the blameless son of Peirous,
Rhigmus, who from rich-soiled Thrace had come;
sentences.i: Then he set out after the blameless son of Peirous, Rhigmus, who had come from rich-soiled Thrace;
sentences.n: αὐτὰρ ὃ βῆ ῥ’ ἰέναι ‘but he set out to go’ (βῆ the aorist of βαίνω, ἰέναι ‘to go’). μετ’ ἀμύμονα Πείρεω υἱὸν Ῥίγμον ‘after the blameless son of Peirous, Rhigmus’: μετά takes the accusative ‘after, in pursuit of’; Πείρεω is the genitive of the name Πείρως. ἀμύμων ‘blameless’ is a stock epithet, translated every time; its sense is not known. ὃς ἐκ Θρῄκης ἐριβώλακος εἰληλούθει ‘who from rich-soiled Thrace had come’: ἐριβώλαξ ‘rich-soiled’, and εἰληλούθει the pluperfect of ἔρχομαι.

sentences.t:
τὸν βάλε μέσσον ἄκοντι, πάγη δ’ ἐν νηδύϊ χαλκός,
ἤριπε δ’ ἐξ ὀχέων·
sentences.l:
him he struck in the middle with a javelin, and fixed in the belly was the bronze,
and he crashed down from the chariot;
sentences.i: He struck him in the middle with a javelin, and the bronze stuck fast in his belly, and Rigmus crashed down from his chariot;
sentences.n: τὸν βάλε μέσσον ἄκοντι ‘him he struck in the middle with a javelin’. πάγη is the aorist passive (second) of πήγνυμι ‘fix, fasten’, with ἐν νηδύϊ ‘in the belly’ and χαλκός ‘the bronze’, the weapon. ἤριπε δ’ ἐξ ὀχέων ‘and he crashed down from the chariot’: ἤριπε the aorist of ἐρείπω, ὀχέων the genitive plural of ὄχος ‘chariot’.

sentences.t:
ὃ δ’ Ἀρηΐθοον θεράποντα
ἂψ ἵππους στρέψαντα μετάφρενον ὀξέϊ δουρὶ
νύξ’, ἀπὸ δ’ ἅρματος ὦσε· κυκήθησαν δέ οἱ ἵπποι.
sentences.l:
and Areithous, the attendant,
as he turned the horses back, in the back with a sharp spear
stabbed, and from the chariot thrust him; and thrown into confusion were his horses.
sentences.i: And as his attendant Areithous was turning the horses back, he stabbed him in the back with a sharp spear and pushed him from the chariot; and his horses were thrown into confusion.
sentences.n: This unit begins in the middle of line 487. Ἀρηΐθοον θεράποντα is ‘Areithous, the attendant’ (the two words name the same man, Rigmus’ driver); θεράπων is ‘attendant’. ἂψ ἵππους στρέψαντα ‘having turned the horses back’ (aorist participle of στρέφω). μετάφρενον ὀξέϊ δουρί ‘in the back with a sharp spear’; νύξ’ is the aorist of νύσσω ‘stab’. ἀπὸ δ’ ἅρματος ὦσε ‘and thrust him from the chariot’ (ἀπό with ἅρματος). κυκήθησαν is the aorist passive of κυκάω ‘stir up’, ‘were thrown into confusion’; οἱ ‘his’.

sentences.t:
ὡς δ’ ἀναμαιμάει βαθέ’ ἄγκεα θεσπιδαὲς πῦρ
οὔρεος ἀζαλέοιο, βαθεῖα δὲ καίεται ὕλη,
πάντῃ τε κλονέων ἄνεμος φλόγα εἰλυφάζει,
sentences.l:
And as through deep glens wondrous-blazing fire rages
on a dry mountain, and the deep forest burns,
and everywhere the wind, throwing it into confusion, swirls the flame,
sentences.i: As wondrous-blazing fire rages through the deep glens of a dry mountain, and the deep forest burns, and the wind, throwing it into confusion on every side, swirls the flame about,
sentences.n: A simile opens. ὡς δ’ is ‘and as’. ἀναμαιμάει is a rare verb of fire and rage; its exact sense is not known, and ‘rages through’ is taken from the context. βαθέ’ ἄγκεα ‘deep glens’ is its object (βαθέ’ = βαθέα). θεσπιδαὲς πῦρ ‘wondrous-blazing fire’ is a stock phrase, translated every time. οὔρεος ἀζαλέοιο ‘of a dry mountain’ (οὖρος = ὄρος; ἀζαλέος ‘dry’). βαθεῖα … ὕλη ‘deep forest’; καίεται ‘burns’. πάντῃ ‘every way’; κλονέων is the present participle of κλονέω ‘throw into confusion’. εἰλυφάζει is a rare verb (‘swirls, rolls’, from the context). The comparison is completed at 493.

sentences.t:
ὣς ὅ γε πάντῃ θῦνε σὺν ἔγχεϊ δαίμονι ἶσος
κτεινομένους ἐφέπων·
sentences.l:
so he everywhere rushed with his spear, equal to a divinity,
pursuing men as they were killed;
sentences.i: so Achilles rushed everywhere with his spear, like a divinity, pursuing men as they were killed;
sentences.n: ὣς ὅ γε ‘so he’ completes the simile with Achilles as subject. θῦνε is the imperfect of θύνω ‘rush’; σὺν ἔγχεϊ ‘with his spear’; δαίμονι ἶσος ‘equal to a divinity’. κτεινομένους ἐφέπων ‘pursuing men as they were killed’: κτεινομένους is the present passive participle of κτείνω ‘kill’, and ἐφέπων the present participle of ἐφέπω ‘pursue, follow after’.

sentences.t: ῥέε δ’ αἵματι γαῖα μέλαινα.
sentences.l: and with blood ran the dark earth.
sentences.i: and the dark earth ran with blood.
sentences.n: This unit begins in the middle of line 494. ῥέε is the imperfect of ῥέω ‘flow’; αἵματι ‘with blood’; γαῖα μέλαινα ‘the dark earth’ is a stock phrase, translated every time (μέλας is ‘dark’ of the earth).

sentences.t:
ὡς δ’ ὅτε τις ζεύξῃ βόας ἄρσενας εὐρυμετώπους
τριβέμεναι κρῖ λευκὸν ἐϋκτιμένῃ ἐν ἀλωῇ,
ῥίμφά τε λέπτ’ ἐγένοντο βοῶν ὑπὸ πόσσ’ ἐριμύκων,
sentences.l:
And as when someone yokes male oxen, broad-browed,
to rub white barley on a well-built threshing-floor,
and lightly it becomes fine under the feet of the loud-bellowing oxen,
sentences.i: As when a man yokes broad-browed male oxen to thresh white barley on a well-built threshing-floor, and lightly it is made fine under the feet of the loud-bellowing oxen,
sentences.n: A second simile. ὡς δ’ ὅτε τις ζεύξῃ ‘and as when someone yokes’: ζεύξῃ is the aorist subjunctive of ζεύγνυμι. βόας ἄρσενας εὐρυμετώπους ‘male oxen, broad-browed’ (εὐρυμέτωπος ‘broad-browed’). τριβέμεναι is an epic infinitive of τρίβω ‘rub’, here ‘rub out the grain’, i.e. thresh; κρῖ λευκόν ‘white barley’. ἐϋκτιμένῃ ἐν ἀλωῇ ‘on a well-built threshing-floor’ (ἐϋκτίμενος ‘well-built’; ἀλωή ‘threshing-floor’ here, since the grain is being rubbed out on it; elsewhere the word is an orchard or garden). ῥίμφά τε λέπτ’ ἐγένοντο ‘and lightly it (the grain) becomes fine’: λέπτ’ is the neuter plural of λεπτός ‘fine’, ἐγένοντο the aorist of γίγνομαι, an aorist of what regularly happens, so a present in English. βοῶν ὑπὸ πόσσ’ ἐριμύκων ‘under the feet of the loud-bellowing oxen’ (πόσσ’ = ποσσί, dative plural of πούς; ἐρίμυκος ‘loud-bellowing’).

sentences.t:
ὣς ὑπ’ Ἀχιλλῆος μεγαθύμου μώνυχες ἵπποι
στεῖβον ὁμοῦ νέκυάς τε καὶ ἀσπίδας·
sentences.l:
so under great-hearted Achilles the solid-hoofed horses
trampled together dead men and shields;
sentences.i: so, under great-hearted Achilles, the solid-hoofed horses trampled dead men and shields together;
sentences.n: ὣς ὑπ’ Ἀχιλλῆος μεγαθύμου ‘so under great-hearted Achilles’ completes the simile, with the horses driven by him; μεγάθυμος ‘great-hearted’ is a stock epithet, translated every time. μώνυχες ἵπποι ‘solid-hoofed horses’ is a stock phrase, translated every time (μώνυξ ‘with an undivided hoof’). στεῖβον is the imperfect of στείβω ‘tread, trample’; ὁμοῦ ‘together’; νέκυάς τε καὶ ἀσπίδας ‘dead men and shields’ (νέκυς ‘dead man’).

sentences.t:
αἵματι δ’ ἄξων
νέρθεν ἅπας πεπάλακτο καὶ ἄντυγες αἳ περὶ δίφρον,
ἃς ἄρ’ ἀφ’ ἱππείων ὁπλέων ῥαθάμιγγες ἔβαλλον
αἵ τ’ ἀπ’ ἐπισσώτρων·
sentences.l:
and with blood the axle
underneath was all spattered, and the rails that run around the chariot,
which the drops from the horses’ hooves struck
and those from the tires.
sentences.i: and the axle underneath was all spattered with blood, and the rails around the chariot, which drops from the horses’ hooves struck, and those from the tires.
sentences.n: This unit begins in the middle of line 499. αἵματι δ’ ἄξων νέρθεν ἅπας πεπάλακτο ‘and the axle underneath was all spattered with blood’: πεπάλακτο is the pluperfect passive of παλάσσω ‘spatter’; νέρθεν ‘underneath’, ἅπας ‘all’. ἄντυγες αἳ περὶ δίφρον ‘the rails around the chariot’ (ἄντυξ ‘rail’, the rim of the chariot-body). ἃς ἄρ’ ἀφ’ ἱππείων ὁπλέων ῥαθάμιγγες ἔβαλλον ‘which drops from the horses’ hooves struck’ (ῥάθαμιγξ ‘drop’, ὁπλαί ‘hooves’), αἵ τ’ ἀπ’ ἐπισσώτρων ‘and those from the tires’ (ἐπίσσωτρον ‘tire’ of the wheel).

sentences.t:
ὃ δὲ ἵετο κῦδος ἀρέσθαι
Πηλεΐδης, λύθρῳ δὲ παλάσσετο χεῖρας ἀάπτους.
sentences.l:
and he was eager to win glory,
Peleus’-son, and with gore was spattered, as to the hands, untouchable.
sentences.i: and Peleus’ son was eager to win glory, and his irresistible hands were spattered with gore.
sentences.n: This unit begins in the middle of line 502. ὃ δὲ ἵετο κῦδος ἀρέσθαι ‘and he was eager to win glory’: ἵετο is the imperfect of ἵεμαι ‘be eager’, ἀρέσθαι the aorist infinitive of ἄρνυμαι ‘win’, and Πηλεΐδης ‘Peleus’ son’ is the subject. λύθρῳ δὲ παλάσσετο χεῖρας ἀάπτους ‘and with gore was spattered, as to the hands, untouchable’: λύθρον is blood and dirt together, ‘gore’; παλάσσετο the imperfect passive of παλάσσω; χεῖρας ἀάπτους an accusative of respect. ἀάπτους is a word of unknown meaning; ‘untouchable’ / ‘irresistible’ are traditional guesses.
